content: 1. Increased plasma levels of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 can occur due to interactions with other substances. 2. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, thereby reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 4. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin degludec via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Norethindrone acetate also reduces the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance, potentially affecting glycemic control. 7. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of both insulin degludec and insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of insulin degludec and insulin aspart via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are required. 9. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of insulin detemir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of inhaled insulin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, potentially affecting glycemic control. 12. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of insulin glargine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 19. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as itraconazole, may elevate plasma hormone levels. 21. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. 23. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole, may elevate plasma hormone levels. 25. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 26. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. 27. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. 31. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of liraglutide via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 36. Norethindrone acetate increases the levels of maraviroc by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary due to the potential for increased toxicity. 37.
